posts.hook: Dua produk 'herba' dibatalkan NPRA dalam tempoh dua bulan. Sebabnya bukan kunyit.

bm.instagram:
Saqa Glowing Turmeric Night Treatment Cream dibatalkan notifikasinya oleh NPRA pada 9 Februari 2026. Sebab: merkuri. Glowing Herbal Treatment pula dibatalkan pada 2 April 2026, sebab merkuri dan betamethasone 17-valerate. Kenyataan Media KKM 9 Februari 2026 dan 2 April 2026

Pattern yang kita nampak selepas semak senarai pembatalan NPRA: kedua-dua produk pakai perkataan 'turmeric' dan 'herbal' pada label. Tapi bahan yang dikesan bukan kunyit, bahan yang dikesan logam berat dan steroid.

Ini bukan kebetulan pemasaran. Kesan cerah yang pantas dan ketara, yang pengguna nampak dalam beberapa hari, datang daripada merkuri dan steroid, bukan daripada kunyit. Nama 'herba' pada label berfungsi untuk jelaskan kenapa kesan tu laju, supaya pengguna tak syak apa-apa.

Kalau anda jenama yang betul-betul guna ekstrak botani, kunyit sebenar, ni bukan cerita orang lain punya masalah. Anda kongsi rak yang sama dengan produk macam ni. Kalau anda tak simpan CoA dan heavy metal test untuk setiap batch, pengguna dan pihak berkuasa tak ada cara nak bezakan jenama anda dengan jenama yang baru kena tarik notifikasi.

Simpan CoA. Uji logam berat setiap batch. Itu je yang boleh cakap bagi pihak anda bila soalan mula datang.

Kalau anda jenama botani sebenar, anda kongsi rak dengan produk macam ni. Simpan CoA dan uji logam berat setiap batch, itu je yang boleh buktikan beza anda.

Bukan kunyit yang buat kulit cerah pantas. Merkuri yang buat.

Kalau jenama anda guna ekstrak botani betul, simpan CoA dan ujian logam berat setiap batch. Rak yang sama, produk yang beza.

en.instagram:
Saqa Glowing Turmeric Night Treatment Cream had its notification cancelled by NPRA on 9 February 2026. Reason: mercury. Glowing Herbal Treatment was cancelled on 2 April 2026, for mercury and betamethasone 17-valerate. Kenyataan Media KKM, 9 February 2026 and 2 April 2026

The pattern we noticed after checking NPRA's cancellation list: both products use the words 'turmeric' and 'herbal' on the label. But what got detected in testing wasn't turmeric, it was heavy metal and a steroid.

This isn't marketing coincidence. The fast, visible skin lightening effect users saw within days comes from mercury and steroids, not from turmeric. The 'herbal' branding exists to explain why the effect was so quick, without raising suspicion.

If you run a brand that genuinely uses botanical extract, real turmeric, this isn't someone else's problem. You share shelf space with products like this. Without a CoA and heavy metal testing on every batch, there's no way for consumers or regulators to tell your brand apart from one that just got its notification pulled.

Keep the CoA. Test heavy metals every batch. That's the only thing that speaks for you when the questions start.

posts.hook: 'Nasi Lemak' atau 'Nasi Kandar' atas papan tanda bukan jaminan halal, itu cuma nama masakan.

bm.instagram:
Isu yang tular baru-baru ini pasal restoran jual Nasi Lemak Babi bersebelahan Nasi Kandar Babi buat ramai keliru. Ramai fikir nama pinggan tradisional macam ni automatik bawa maksud halal sebab makanan ni memang associated dengan masakan Melayu.

Tapi dari segi undang-undang, nama masakan dan pengisytiharan halal adalah dua benda berasingan. 'Nasi Lemak' atau 'Nasi Kandar' adalah nama resipi, bukan halal claim. Restoran boleh guna nama itu untuk versi apa-apa lauk sekalipun, termasuk daging babi, selagi mereka tak letak label atau iklan 'halal' tanpa sijil sah dari JAKIM atau JAIN negeri.

Trade Descriptions Act 2011 (Certification and Marking of Halal) Order yang kawal bila sesuatu premis boleh guna perkataan 'halal' secara rasmi, bukan nama pinggan itu sendiri.

Untuk pengusaha yang memang 100% halal pula, ini pengajaran penting: nama pinggan generik tak cukup untuk beritahu pelanggan Muslim premis anda berbeza. Papan tanda yang jelas dan sijil SPHM yang displayed di premise kekal cara paling pasti pelanggan boleh tahu beza anda dengan kedai sebelah yang guna nama sama tapi tak halal.

JAKIM, “Penjelasan Isu Nasi Lemak Babi dan Nasi Kandar Babi” (Isu-Isu Tular Halal)
bm.facebook:
Restoran jual Nasi Lemak Babi sebelah Nasi Kandar Babi buat ramai keliru minggu ni. Fakta: nama pinggan macam 'nasi lemak' atau 'nasi kandar' adalah nama masakan, bukan halal claim. Restoran boleh guna nama tu untuk versi babi pun, selagi tak dakwa halal tanpa sijil.

Untuk premis yang memang halal, nama pinggan sahaja tak cukup. Papan tanda jelas dan sijil SPHM yang displayed kekal cara paling pasti pelanggan Muslim tahu beza premis anda.

JAKIM, “Penjelasan Isu Nasi Lemak Babi dan Nasi Kandar Babi”
bm.threads: Nama pinggan macam 'nasi lemak' bukan halal claim, itu nama masakan je. Restoran boleh jual versi babi guna nama sama, selagi tak dakwa halal tanpa sijil. Kalau anda halal betul, nama pinggan tak cukup, papan tanda dan sijil SPHM yang selesaikan keraguan pelanggan.

en.instagram:
A restaurant selling Pork Nasi Lemak next to Pork Nasi Kandar has been the talk of the town lately, and it's tripped a lot of people up. The assumption: dish names like these carry an implied halal status because they're associated with Malay cuisine.

Legally, that's wrong. The dish name and the halal declaration are two separate things. 'Nasi Lemak' or 'Nasi Kandar' is a recipe name, not a halal claim. A restaurant can use that name for a pork version, a beef version, anything, as long as it does not advertise or label the premise as 'halal' without a valid certificate from JAKIM or a state JAIN.

The Trade Descriptions (Certification and Marking of Halal) Order 2011, paragraph 4(1), governs when a business can officially use the word 'halal', not the dish name itself.

For genuinely halal operators, the lesson cuts the other way: a generic dish name does not tell your Muslim customers anything. Clear signage and a displayed SPHM certificate remain the only reliable way customers can tell your premise apart from the one next door using the same dish name.

JAKIM, “Penjelasan Isu Nasi Lemak Babi dan Nasi Kandar Babi” (Isu-Isu Tular Halal)

Signage and a displayed SPHM certificate will.

posts.hook: A textile standard just borrowed its safety limits from the cosmetics annex, and that is worth noticing.

bm.linkedin:
Kenya dan Komuniti Afrika Timur edarkan draf standard untuk disposable wet wipes (G/TBT/N/KEN/2117, diedarkan 24 September 2026), difailkan di bawah ICS 59.080.01, Textiles.

Tapi senarai dokumen rujukan standard ini sendiri memetik ARS 1524-1/2/3 (senarai bahan dilarang, terhad dan dibenarkan), ISO 23674 (had merkuri dalam kosmetik) dan lima standard ISO lain untuk ujian mikrobiologi kosmetik.

Jadi tajuk klasifikasi Textiles tidak bermakna produk itu terlepas daripada had bahan dan mikrobiologi gred kosmetik. Rujukan normatif standard itu sendiri yang menentukan, bukan ICS code di muka depan.

Untuk sesiapa yang failkan produk berasaskan klasifikasi tunggal, rujukan silang dalam standard yang dipakai kena disemak dulu, bukan sekadar tajuk dan kod ICS.

Tingkap maklum balas tutup 23 November 2026.

Sources: Kenya/East African Community, Draft African Standard, Disposable wet wipes - Specification, G/TBT/N/KEN/2117, WTO TBT notification, distributed 24 Sept 2026

#RegulatoryAffairs #WTOTBT #CosmeticSafety #StandardsCompliance

en.linkedin:
A textile standard just borrowed its safety limits from the cosmetics annex, and that is worth noticing.

Kenya and the East African Community notified a draft standard for disposable wet wipes (G/TBT/N/KEN/2117, distributed 24 September 2026), filed under ICS 59.080.01, Textiles.

Its own reference document list cites ARS 1524-1/2/3 (prohibited, restricted and permitted substance lists), ISO 23674 and five further ISO standards for cosmetic microbiology test methods.

A Textiles classification heading does not mean the product escapes cosmetic-grade substance and microbiology limits. The standard's own normative references decide that, not the ICS code on the cover page.

If you file a product outside cosmetic scope on the strength of a classification heading alone, check the reference list the standard actually cites first.

Comment window closes 23 November 2026.

Sources: Kenya/East African Community, Draft African Standard, Disposable wet wipes - Specification, G/TBT/N/KEN/2117, WTO TBT notification, distributed 24 Sept 2026

posts.hook: Papan tanda halal, warna hijau kedai, nama Melayu, menu tanpa babi: bukan satu pun pengesahan status SPHM.

bm.instagram:
Papan tanda "halal", warna hijau kedai, nama syarikat yang berbunyi Melayu, menu tanpa babi: bukan satu pun daripada itu adalah pengesahan status halal sesebuah premis.

Ramai confuse antara "nampak halal" dengan "ada SPHM" (Sijil Pengesahan Halal Malaysia). Dua benda berbeza. Premis boleh letak apa sahaja label sendiri kat depan kedai, tiada siapa halang. Yang sah cuma satu: adakah nama syarikat dan cawangan tu ada dalam senarai pemegang SPHM JAKIM.

Cara semak, ambil masa kurang satu minit:
1. Pergi Portal Halal Malaysia atau sistem MYeHALAL
2. Search guna nama syarikat berdaftar, bukan nama jenama pasaran
3. Check status setiap cawangan, sebab satu syarikat boleh ada cawangan bersijil dan cawangan tak bersijil serentak
4. Kalau tak jumpa, itu jawapannya: bukan pemegang SPHM

JAKIM sendiri dah jelaskan berkali-kali bila isu tular pasal premis tertentu: premis berkenaan bukan pemegang SPHM dan JAKIM tak pernah keluarkan pensijilan untuk premis itu. Ini status dalam sistem, bukan pendapat orang ramai.

Kalau anda operator, jangan letak apa-apa simbol atau perkataan halal sebelum sijil tu betul-betul dalam tangan anda. Kalau anda consumer, semak dulu sebelum percaya papan tanda.
bm.facebook:
Papan tanda "halal", warna hijau, nama Melayu, menu tanpa babi: bukan satu pun pengesahan status SPHM sesebuah premis.

Status sebenar cuma boleh disahkan melalui Portal Halal Malaysia atau sistem MYeHALAL, ikut nama syarikat dan cawangan, bukan nama jenama. Satu syarikat boleh ada cawangan bersijil dan cawangan tak bersijil serentak.

Bila isu tular, JAKIM selalunya beri jawapan sama: premis bukan pemegang SPHM, JAKIM tak pernah keluarkan pensijilan untuknya. Itu status sistem, bukan pendapat.
bm.threads: Papan tanda halal, warna kedai, nama Melayu, menu tanpa babi: bukan satu pun pengesahan status SPHM. Status sebenar cuma dalam Portal Halal Malaysia dan MYeHALAL, ikut nama syarikat dan cawangan. Satu syarikat boleh ada cawangan bersijil dan tak bersijil serentak. JAKIM dah jelaskan berkali-kali: bila viral, jawapannya sama, premis bukan pemegang SPHM.

en.instagram:
A "halal" signboard, a green shopfront, a Malay-sounding name, a pork-free menu: none of that is proof of SPHM status.

People keep confusing "looks halal" with "holds SPHM" (Sijil Pengesahan Halal Malaysia). A premise can put up whatever wording it wants on its own storefront, nobody stops that. The only thing that settles it is whether the exact registered company name and branch appears in JAKIM's list of SPHM holders.

Checking takes under a minute:
1. Go to Portal Halal Malaysia or the MYeHALAL system
2. Search by the registered company name, not the marketing brand name
3. Check each branch separately, one company can have a certified outlet and an uncertified outlet at the same time
4. If it doesn't show up, that's the answer, not a certificate holder

JAKIM has said this repeatedly when a premise goes viral: not an SPHM holder, JAKIM never issued certification for it. That's a system status, not an opinion.

If you run a premise, don't put up any halal wording or symbol until the certificate is actually in your hand. If you're a consumer, check before you trust the signboard.

posts.hook: A pharmacy counter tester passed preservative efficacy testing once, sealed. It has been opened, touched and re-capped by strangers every day since.

bm.linkedin:
Tester kosmetik di kaunter farmasi lulus preservative efficacy testing sekali sahaja, dalam keadaan sealed. Selepas itu ia dibuka, disentuh dan ditutup semula oleh orang ramai setiap hari.

Kajian pilot dalam Microorganisms (21 September 2026) swab tester kosmetik di farmasi Portugal dan jumpa lebih daripada kontaminasi biasa. Beberapa isolate bawa penanda antimicrobial resistance, bukan sekadar flora kulit normal.

Preservative efficacy testing (challenge testing) sahkan model pendedahan sealed, single-use. Ia tak cakap apa-apa pasal tester yang dibuka setiap hari, jari dicelup berulang kali, selama berbulan-bulan. Sistem pengawet yang lulus PET pada hari pertama sedang lawan pertempuran berbeza pada minggu kedua belas.

Kalau produk anda ada dalam bentuk tester kaunter, open-life stability dan beban mikrob selepas penggunaan berulang patut ada data sendiri, bukan andaian yang dipinjam daripada keputusan pek sealed.

Sources: Ribeiro S, Silva JD, Pacheco P. In-Store Cosmetic Testers Harbour Resistant Bacteria: A Pilot Survey of Microbial Contamination and Antimicrobial Susceptibility in Portuguese Pharmacies. Microorganisms, 21 September 2026. DOI: 10.3390/microorganisms14092120

#CosmeticScience #Preservation #Cosmetovigilance #RegulatoryAffairs #QualityControl

en.linkedin:
A pharmacy counter tester passed preservative efficacy testing once, sealed. It has been opened, touched and re-capped by strangers every day since.

A pilot study in Microorganisms (21 September 2026) swabbed in-store cosmetic testers across Portuguese pharmacies and found more than contamination. Several isolates carried antimicrobial resistance markers, not just the expected skin flora.

Preservative efficacy testing (challenge testing) validates a sealed, single-use exposure model. It says nothing about a tester that gets opened daily, fingers dipped in repeatedly, for months. The preservative system that passed PET on day one is fighting a different battle by week twelve.

If your product ships as a counter tester, the open-life stability and microbial load after repeated use deserve their own data point, not an assumption borrowed from the sealed-pack result.

Sources: Ribeiro S, Silva JD, Pacheco P. In-Store Cosmetic Testers Harbour Resistant Bacteria: A Pilot Survey of Microbial Contamination and Antimicrobial Susceptibility in Portuguese Pharmacies. Microorganisms, 21 September 2026. DOI: 10.3390/microorganisms14092120

#CosmeticScience #Preservation #Cosmetovigilance #RegulatoryAffairs #QualityControl

posts.hook: Oreo 'mengandungi lemak babi' tular lagi. JAKIM dah jawab. Tapi ramai masih tersasar poin sebenar.

bm.instagram:
Dakwaan Oreo ada lemak dan susu babi kembali tular. Dalam halaman Isu-Isu Tular Halal rasmi JAKIM, sudah dijelaskan: produk itu dihasilkan oleh Mondelez Indonesia Manufacturing dan disijilkan halal oleh BPJPH (Badan Penyelenggara Jaminan Produk Halal), Kementerian Agama Republik Indonesia, iaitu salah satu badan pensijilan halal luar negara yang diiktiraf JAKIM.

Tapi bab ni yang selalu tersasar bila cakap pasal produk import: anda tak perlu sijil JAKIM untuk produk itu sah halal di Malaysia. Yang anda perlukan ialah sijil daripada badan pensijilan yang berada dalam senarai pengiktirafan JAKIM.

Dan tu bukan semakan sekali sahaja. Kerja due diligence anda sebagai pengimport atau peruncit ada dua lapis:

1. Sijil produk itu sendiri sah dan masih dalam tempoh.
2. Badan yang mengeluarkan sijil tu masih berstatus diiktiraf pada tarikh anda mengimport, bukan pada tarikh sijil dikeluarkan.

Status pengiktirafan boleh berubah. Kalau anda import produk luar negara dan letak label halal atas rak tanpa semak dua-dua lapis ni, risiko tu bukan pada jenama asal, risiko tu jatuh atas anda sebagai peruncit di Malaysia.
bm.facebook:
Isu Oreo tular semula: dakwaan ada lemak babi. JAKIM dah jawab dalam halaman Isu-Isu Tular Halal rasminya, produk itu disijilkan halal oleh BPJPH di Indonesia, badan yang diiktiraf JAKIM.

Poin sebenar untuk pengimport: produk import tak perlu sijil JAKIM, tapi perlu sijil daripada badan yang masih dalam senarai pengiktirafan JAKIM. Dua lapis semakan: sijil sah, dan badan tu masih diiktiraf pada tarikh import, bukan tarikh sijil dikeluarkan.
bm.threads:
Oreo tular lagi pasal 'lemak babi'. JAKIM dah jawab: BPJPH Indonesia yang sijilkan, badan diiktiraf JAKIM.

Poin yang ramai terlepas: produk import bukan perlu sijil JAKIM, tapi sijil dari badan dalam senarai diiktiraf. Dan semakan tu dua lapis, bukan satu.

en.instagram:
The Oreo 'contains pork fat and lard' claim is circulating again. JAKIM's own Isu-Isu Tular Halal page addressed it directly: the product is manufactured by Mondelez Indonesia Manufacturing and certified halal by BPJPH (Badan Penyelenggara Jaminan Produk Halal) under Indonesia's Ministry of Religious Affairs, one of the foreign halal certification bodies recognized by JAKIM.

Here is the part importers and retailers keep missing: an imported product does not need a JAKIM certificate to be halal-valid in Malaysia. It needs a certificate from a body that sits on JAKIM's recognition list.

That check has two layers, not one:

1. The product certificate itself is valid and current.
2. The issuing body is still on JAKIM's recognized list as of the date you import, not the date the certificate was issued.

Recognition status can change. If you're bringing in foreign products and putting a halal label on the shelf without checking both layers, that risk sits with you as the Malaysian retailer, not the original brand.
en.facebook:
The Oreo pork fat claim is circulating again. JAKIM's Isu-Isu Tular Halal page already addressed it: the product is certified by BPJPH Indonesia, a body recognized by JAKIM.

The real point for importers: you don't need a JAKIM certificate on an imported product, you need one from a body still on JAKIM's recognition list. That's two checks, not one: the certificate is valid, and the body is still recognized on your import date.
en.threads:
Oreo pork claim again. JAKIM already answered: BPJPH Indonesia certified it, a body JAKIM recognizes.

What importers miss: no JAKIM cert needed, just one from a recognized body. And that's two checks, not one.

posts.hook: Kalau produk herba itu betul-betul berkesan dalam tiga hari, tanya bahan apa yang dicampur.

bm.instagram:
Kalau produk herba itu betul-betul berkesan dalam tiga hari, tanya bahan apa yang dicampur.

Senarai produk semula jadi dan tradisional yang dibatalkan pendaftaran NPRA tunjukkan corak yang sangat konsisten. Produk 'tenaga batin' yang dibatalkan selalunya mengandungi sildenafil atau tadalafil. Produk 'kencing manis' mengandungi glibenclamide. Produk sakit sendi mengandungi methyl salicylate dan thymol dalam kuantiti tak diisytiharkan. Plaster ubat mengandungi diphenhydramine. PS 21 Capsule (MAL15120007TC) dibatalkan kerana simvastatin.

Perhatikan corak ini: setiap bahan yang dicampur adalah ubat farmaseutikal yang tepat sepadan dengan dakwaan produk itu. Ini bukan pencemaran tidak sengaja semasa proses pengeluaran. Ini reka bentuk formulasi supaya pengguna rasa kesan cepat, tanpa tahu apa yang mereka telan.

Untuk pengusaha yang jual produk herba sebenar tanpa campuran ini, inilah sebab pelanggan anda skeptikal walaupun produk anda bersih. Dan inilah sebab nombor MAL anda bermakna: ia boleh disemak di laman NPRA, dan produk yang dibatalkan keluar dari senarai berdaftar.

en.instagram:
If an herbal product actually works in three days, ask what's been mixed in.

NPRA's list of cancelled natural and traditional product registrations shows a very consistent pattern. Cancelled 'stamina' products usually contain sildenafil or tadalafil. Cancelled 'diabetes' products contain glibenclamide. Joint pain products contain undeclared quantities of methyl salicylate and thymol. Medicated plasters contain diphenhydramine. PS 21 Capsule (MAL15120007TC) was cancelled for simvastatin.

Notice the pattern: every adulterant is a pharmaceutical that matches the product's claim exactly. This isn't accidental contamination during manufacturing. It's formulation by design, so users feel fast results without knowing what they've swallowed.

For SMEs selling genuine herbal products without this, this is why your customers are skeptical even when your product is clean. And this is why your MAL number matters: it's checkable on NPRA's site, and cancelled products drop off that list.

posts.hook: A Margin of Safety calculation needs a dermal absorption value. Most files borrow one instead of measuring it.

bm.linkedin:
Kiraan Margin of Safety perlukan nilai dermal absorption. Kebanyakan fail pinjam nilai tu, bukan ukur sendiri.

Kajian in vitro baharu dalam Food and Chemical Toxicology (25 September 2026) ukur dermal absorption sebenar Lauryl Isoquinolinium Bromide, bahan antimicrobial quaternary yang digunakan dalam sesetengah format leave-on dan rinse-off, daripada matrix krim sebenar, bukan larutan neat.

Metodologi SCCS benarkan default absorption fraction bila tiada data terukur, dan default tu memang sengaja conservative. Nilai terukur daripada matrix produk siap sebenar boleh ubah systemic exposure dose yang digunakan dalam formula MoS dengan ketara, ke dua-dua arah, sebab absorption melalui kulit bergantung pada vehicle, bukan setakat molekul sahaja.

Kalau PIF anda masih pakai andaian default absorption untuk active yang ada data in vitro yang sudah diterbitkan, itu bukan jalan pintas, itu nombor yang lebih lemah duduk di tempat nombor yang lebih kuat sudah wujud.

Sources: Kim JW, Kim HY, Chung HN. In vitro dermal absorption of Lauryl Isoquinolinium Bromide (LIB) from a cosmetic cream formulation. Food and Chemical Toxicology, 25 September 2026. DOI: 10.1016/j.fct.2026.116406

#RegulatoryAffairs #CosmeticScience #SafetyAssessment #MarginOfSafety #SCCS

en.linkedin:
A Margin of Safety calculation needs a dermal absorption value. Most files borrow one instead of measuring it.

A new in vitro study in Food and Chemical Toxicology (25 September 2026) measured actual dermal absorption of Lauryl Isoquinolinium Bromide, a quaternary antimicrobial used in some leave-on and rinse-off cosmetic formats, from a real cream matrix rather than a neat solution.

The SCCS methodology allows a default absorption fraction when no measured data exists, and that default is deliberately conservative. A measured value from the actual finished-product matrix can shift the systemic exposure dose used in the MoS formula considerably, in either direction, because absorption through skin depends on the vehicle, not just the molecule.

If your PIF still carries a default absorption assumption for an active with published in vitro data available, that is not a shortcut, it is a weaker number sitting where a stronger one already exists.

Sources: Kim JW, Kim HY, Chung HN. In vitro dermal absorption of Lauryl Isoquinolinium Bromide (LIB) from a cosmetic cream formulation. Food and Chemical Toxicology, 25 September 2026. DOI: 10.1016/j.fct.2026.116406

#RegulatoryAffairs #CosmeticScience #SafetyAssessment #MarginOfSafety #SCCS

posts.hook: Rempah kari tular sebab video WhatsApp, tapi titik kawalan sebenar langsung bukan di situ.

bm.instagram:
JAKIM dah keluarkan penjelasan rasmi dalam laman Isu-Isu Tular Halal berkenaan video dan mesej WhatsApp yang mendakwa rempah kari dan kurma import dari India dihasilkan guna najis dan air kencing lembu. Penemuan JAKIM: produk yang dipersoalkan itu tidak memiliki SPHM, dan tiada juga sijil daripada badan pensijilan halal luar negara yang diiktiraf.

Itu penemuan sebenar, bukan tuduhan yang tular tu.

Untuk premis makanan, ini bahagian yang penting dan selalu tercicir: bahan yang tiada sijil diiktiraf bukan automatik haram. Statusnya cuma tak dapat disahkan. Dua perkara tu berbeza. Tapi bila premis anda bersijil, bahan yang statusnya tak dapat disahkan pun sama je kesannya, tak boleh guna.

Anda boleh ada SPHM tergantung depan kaunter dan tetap gagal audit sebab satu tin rempah kari di dapur belakang tiada dokumen sokongan. Auditor tak tanya pasal rasa. Dia tanya sijil dan asal bahan, sampai ke pembekal.

Due diligence bermula dari invois pembekal, bukan dari label produk siap. Kalau pembekal tak boleh tunjukkan sijil halal yang sah atau nombor MYeHALAL, bahan tu keluar dari senarai bahan mentah premis bersijil, walaupun ia sendiri tak haram.

Itu penemuan sebenarnya, bukan dakwaan najis yang tular.

Untuk premis makanan: bahan tanpa sijil diiktiraf bukan automatik haram, statusnya cuma tak dapat disahkan. Tapi premis bersijil tetap tak boleh guna. SPHM depan kaunter tak selamatkan anda kalau satu bahan di dapur belakang tiada dokumen.

en.instagram:
JAKIM published an official clarification on its Isu-Isu Tular Halal page about the Facebook video and WhatsApp messages claiming that imported Indian curry spices and dates were produced using cow dung and urine. JAKIM's actual finding: the questioned products carried no SPHM and no certificate from a recognised foreign halal certification body.

That is the real finding, not the claim that went viral.

For food premises, here is the part that keeps getting missed: an ingredient without a recognised certificate is not automatically haram. Its status simply cannot be verified. Those are two different things. But once your premise holds SPHM, an ingredient with unverifiable status gets treated the same way as one that fails, it cannot be used.

You can have SPHM hanging at the counter and still fail an audit because one tin of curry powder in the back kitchen has no supporting documentation. The auditor is not asking about taste. They are asking for certificates, traced back to the supplier.

Due diligence starts at the supplier invoice, not the finished product label. If a supplier cannot produce a valid halal certificate or a MYeHALAL number, that ingredient comes off the list for a certified premise, even if it is not haram on its own.

That's the actual finding, not the dung and urine claim that went around on WhatsApp.

For food premises: no recognised certificate does not mean haram, it means unverified. But a certified premise still can't use it. SPHM at the counter won't save you if one ingredient in the back kitchen has no paper trail.
